payload.title: scripts/migrations/ has zero tsc coverage project-wide -> type errors ship silently
payload.problem: scripts/migrations/ is outside the include globs of BOTH the root tsconfig.json and apps/mcp-server/tsconfig.json, so the project check (pnpm --filter vn-market check) never type-checks any file in that directory. A router 'tsc-clean' claim on such a script is false-clean-by-omission — the real check silently skips it.
payload.evidence: QA built an isolated tsconfig with the project's pinned compiler (tsc 5.9.3) and found: (1) discover-consolidated-bctc-pdf.ts:395 — new Blob([pdfBytes],...) : Uint8Array<ArrayBufferLike> not assignable to BlobPart (the file HPG-DISCOVER just shipped, commit 90c975415); (2) control-check of the sibling it mirrors, reparse-bctc-reports.ts (already shipped), surfaced 2 of ITS OWN pre-existing type errors. Confirms the gap is directory-wide and pre-existing, not a regression unique to one task.
payload.impact: Zero runtime impact today (Bun strips types at execution; both scripts already ran successfully live). Risk is future: type errors in migration/one-shot scripts ship undetected, and any dev/router claim of 'tsc-clean' for scripts/migrations/ is unverifiable via the standard check.
payload.recommended: Design choice -> PO/architect triage: (a) add scripts/migrations/ to an existing tsconfig include (or a dedicated scripts tsconfig) so pnpm check covers it; OR (b) a lightweight standalone `tsc --noEmit` pass over scripts/ wired into the check/CI gate. Then fix the 3 surfaced errors. PLAN-ONLY — no code change dispatched from this signal.
